scope_statement: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9-1) Religious Studies B (1RB0) 'Beliefs in Action', specification Issue 2, January 2024. This build covers four religion-area options only: Area of Study 1 (Religion and Ethics) for Christianity and for Catholic Christianity, and Area of Study 2 (Religion, Peace and Conflict) for Islam and for Judaism. Each unit teaches that area's four content sections for that religion and nothing else. Area of Study 3 (Religion, Philosophy and Social Justice) content - philosophy of religion, equality - is OUT OF SCOPE and must not be taught as assessed material, and neither is a section from the wrong area (Marriage and the Family belongs to Area of Study 1 only; Crime and Punishment and Peace and Conflict to Area of Study 2 only). There is no non-exam assessment, no coursework and no set text. The lesson's own quoted content points are the scope of that lesson.
factcheck_system_extra: This is a religious studies lesson. Check scripture and source references especially hard: a named chapter-and-verse reference must really say what the lesson claims, a quotation must be real and correctly attributed to the tradition that owns it, and a teaching must belong to the tradition named (do not let a Catholic teaching be given as a general Christian one, an Orthodox Jewish view as a Reform one, or a Sunni practice as a Shi'a one). The specification names particular passages for particular points; a lesson that cites a different passage as the specification's is a MEDIUM finding, and one that cites a passage which does not say what is claimed is HIGH. Treat 'divergent' views as required content: where the lesson gives one voice for a religion the specification asks to be shown as divided, that is a MEDIUM finding on coverage. Be respectful and precise about living traditions.
